comment: Height-above-ground bands, and the ASPRS class each one implies.
READ BY BOTH SIDES OF THE PIPELINE, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS JSON.
pipeline/thresholds.py reads this file to build the PDAL filters.assign
statements that do the classifying; src/config/asprs.ts imports it to draw
the legend and the height ramp for the same data. If these two ever
disagreed, the viewer would confidently mislabel what the pipeline wrote,
so they are not allowed to be two files.
IN METRES, ALWAYS. The sample survey is in FEET and a crop scan may be in
either, so a threshold written in file units is a threshold that is wrong
for the next file. thresholds.py divides by the scan's unitsToMetres (the
same number src/config/scans.ts already carries, read from the file's own
WKT) to reach file units. Nothing anywhere hard-codes feet.
THESE NUMBERS ARE STARTING VALUES AND ARE EXPECTED TO CHANGE. They are
defensible for row crops -- stubble and seedlings under half a metre,
most row crops and canopy between there and five, shelterbelts and trees
above -- but the only scan currently wired up is an aerial survey of a
football stadium, which tests the plumbing and not the agronomy. They
cannot be tuned until a real field scan exists.
